chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Zurara, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Burayd al-Ajli, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever marries a woman solely for her beauty will not find in her what he loves, and whoever marries her solely for her wealth, God will be left to him (or entrusts her to him), so you should marry the woman of religion.'

key_terms.وَكَلَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ: God was left to him / entrusted to him

ai.seo_question: What is the best quality to look for when choosing a spouse in Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the Prophet’s words are contextualized to highlight that exclusive focus on beauty or wealth leads to divine neglect or dissatisfaction, a concept central to Shia marital jurisprudence. The emphasis on 'Dhat al-Din' (one of faith) underscores that spiritual compatibility is the foundation for a stable union, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that piety ensures mutual respect and endurance of marital trials. This hadith is frequently cited in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* to prioritize character over superficial attributes when evaluating potential spouses.
